paper.title: High-fidelity neutral atom gates leveraging low-rank Hessian optimization — Figure 1

model.name: two-atom three-level perfect-blockade CZ model
model.lattice: two identical atoms; seven-state symmetry reduction

method.family: exact Schrödinger propagation plus analytic fidelity Hessian
method.note: The seven-state and symmetry-reduced propagations use identical inputs. The Hessian is checked by independent finite differences. Panel g is a mechanistic reconstruction from the computed two-cycle trajectory; panels h–i test qualitative optimizer ordering.

params.name: time grid
params.why: This is the repository's declared full Figure 1 grid.
params.risk: The winning optimizer endpoint is sensitive below the continuous-propagation resolution.
params.fix: Report the continuous DOP853 result and qualitative ordering; do not claim an exact sub-resolution floor.

params.name: distortion seed
params.why: It makes the reconstructed optimization trajectories deterministic.
params.risk: One seed does not establish a population success probability.
params.fix: Label panels h–i as deterministic mechanistic reconstructions.

params.name: generated panels
params.source: reproduction package plus computed panel-g trajectory
params.why: The full composite now contains all nine paper panel positions.
params.risk: Panel g is a mechanism-level reconstruction, not digitized source data.
params.fix: Label panel g explicitly as a mechanistic reconstruction.

where: local CPU; no usable Slurm profile is configured
risks: Panel g is a computed mechanistic reconstruction rather than digitized paper data.
The published rounded pulse is not an exact CZ in the numerical convention.
Panels h–i are mechanism reconstructions, not digitized experimental curves.

figures.plots: low-rank Hessian geometry and optimization trajectories
figures.x: time, distortion mode, or optimization step
figures.y: control waveform, Hessian sensitivity, or simulated gate error

observe.quantity: Hessian eigenspectrum, principal/null modes, and optimizer trajectories
observe.normalization: trapezoid-normalized waveform modes; computational-subspace average CZ fidelity

figures.expected: The analytic Hessian has rank 5; principal finite-difference curvatures agree with theory, null curvatures are negligible, and the Hessian-coordinate search has the fastest stable qualitative convergence.

results.why: The rank, principal/null modes, and optimizer ordering reproduce the paper's mechanism, but panel g is reconstructed from this run and the rounded analytic pulse is not the authors' exact numerical control.
changes: added panel g from the computed two-cycle Hessian trajectory
